newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks close marginally higher.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks close marginally higher.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed slightly higher Monday in low volume due to the absence of many U.S. investors owing to the U.S. Memorial Day holiday, traders said.

But, dull as trading was, speculation that New York will return to work eager to buy Chilean ADRs Tuesday helped the Santiago Stock Exchange resist the temptation for profit-taking widely predicted before the session opened, traders said.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares ended at 125.34 points, 0.09 percent higher than Friday's close, and the general IGPA index ended at 5495.26 points, up 0.06 percent.
There are high hopes that the market will have a good day tomorrow, with lots of arbitrage with New York,' a trader said, We think that the wave of buying of Chilean ADRs is going to continue.'
He added: "That's why the market ended in a buying mood today, to take positions for Tuesday."

Other bullish factors included rumors that the Central Bank will revise down its signals for May inflation, indicating that it expects a 0.2-percent rise in consumer prices and not a 0.3 percent rise. There are hopes that the Central Bank might lower interest rates, traders said.
Biggest risers were publishing stock Cochrane, up 8.23 percent, metals firm Rebrisa, up 5.14 percent, and telecommunications stock Telex Chile, up 3.67 percent.
The day's losers were mining play Oro Blanco, which slid 3.0 percent, Banco Chile, down 2.83 percent, and Banco BHIF, which lost 2.41 percent.
Volume was an anaemic 8.3 billion pesos, less than a quarter of Friday's turnover.
Rain last week which boosted the prospects of electric stocks with hydro plants helped the Santiago bourse close Friday at its highest level since 1994.
The IPSA ended Friday at 125.22 points, up 1.24 percent, and the IGPA ended 0.82 percent higher at 5491.97 points.
